questions.question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single digit numbers only. Counting to be done from left to right.

(Left) 6 2 5 6 9 1 6 7 6 3 4 7 9 3 7 7 4 5 7 7 6 3 5 6 5 1 3 (Right)

How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
questions.solution:
Given: (Left) 6 2 5 6 9 1 6 7 6 3 4 7 9 3 7 7 4 5 7 7 6 3 5 6 5 1 3 (Right)

Now,

We need to identify odd numbers that are immediately preceded by an odd number and immediately followed by an even number.

So, the required condition is: **Odd Number – Odd Number – Even Number**

(Left) 6 2 5 6 __**9 1 6**__ 7 6 3 4 7 9 3 __**7 7 4**__ 5 **__7 7 6 3 5 6__** 5 1 3 (Right)

Total odd numbers satisfying the condition = 4

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All peas are carrots.

All carrots are turnips.

**Conclusions:**

**(I)** Some turnips are carrots.

**(II)** All peas are turnips.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All peas are carrots.**
All carrots are turnips.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c37424c529075292d68429a66d6bd40ebe7accd188788514b662883cab104008.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some turnips are carrots - Follows **(Since all carrots are turnips, there is definitely an overlap between turnips and carrots).

II. All peas are turnips - Follows (All peas are carrots and all carrots are turnips, so all peas are turnips).

So, both conclusions I and II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

questions.question:
If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

17 D 4 B 3 C 54 A 9 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

Given equation: 17 D 4 B 3 C 54 A 9 = ?

Now, if A stands for ‘÷’, B stands for ‘×’, C stands for ‘+’ and D stands for ‘−’, then:

17 D 4 B 3 C 54 A 9

⇒ 17 − 4 × 3 + 54 ÷ 9

⇒ 17 − 12 + 6

⇒ 5 + 6

⇒ 11

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All hats are mats.

All hats are cats.

All dogs are cats.

**Conclusions:**

(I) All dogs are mats.

(II) Some cats are mats.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All hats are mats.

All hats are cats.

All dogs are cats.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f79defad5faf1bd330931d8534b9af5dc03f700795b6b7ba4107ea42b578a58.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All dogs are mats - **Does not follow** (There is no definite relation between dogs and mats).

II. Some cats are mats - **Follows **(Since all hats are both cats and mats, there is a definite common part between cats and mats).

So, only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question: In a row of 47 people facing north, Umesh is 15th from the right end. If Ketan sits 19th to the left of Umesh, what is Ketan’s position from the left end of the line?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total number of people = 47

Umesh’s position from right = 15th

Ketan sits 19th to the left of Umesh

Ketan’s position from right = 15 + 19 = 34th

Ketan’s position from left = (Total + 1) − Position from right

= (47 + 1) − 34

= 48 − 34

= 14th

Here, Ketan is **14th from the left end** of the line.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(15, 6, 11)

(24, 15, 20)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic:

First number − Second number = 9

Third number − Second number = 5

**(15, 6, 11)**

⇒ 15 − 6 = 9

⇒ 11 − 6 = 5

**(24, 15, 20)**

⇒ 24 − 15 = 9

⇒ 20 − 15 = 5

Now, checking the options:

Option 1) (19, 28, 33)

⇒ 19 − 28 = −9

⇒ 33 − 28 = 5 (does not satisfy both conditions)

**Option 2) (16, 7, 12)**

⇒ 16 − 7 = 9

⇒ 12 − 7 = 5

Option 3) (18, 9, 4)

⇒ 18 − 9 = 9

⇒ 4 − 9 = −5

Option 4) (23, 14, 9)

⇒ 23 − 14 = 9

⇒ 9 − 14 = −5

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

questions.question: Mr. Zzz ranked 14th from the top and 67th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rank from top = 14

Rank from bottom = 67

Total number of students = (Rank from top + Rank from bottom) − 1

= (14 + 67) − 1

= 81 − 1

= 80

Here, there are **80 students** in his class.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
